text: maya: dropping a quick design review thread for the compact roles table iteration. key spots: SSO controls (global vs per-role), inline lock affordance, audit drill-in UX (drawer vs full page), and a11y/copy fixes. link: https://www.figma.com/file/wxyz9876/compact-roles-iter3 - frame 'compact-table-iter3'. sam: got it. first quick thought: per-role SSO toggle in-row feels noisy. can we hide per-role control under the kebab and show an inline lock only when overridden? diego: +1. also recommend the inline lock be decorative by default with `aria-hidden=true` and expose a focusable button in the overflow menu for keyboard users. that avoids tab bloat in the table. lucy: a11y catch: decorative icons still need text alternatives for screen reader users when they convey state. if icon is `aria-hidden`, provide a visually-hidden label in the row like `SSO required for Billing` when applicable. priya: copy suggestion for global toggle: instead of "Enforce SSO for organization", try "Require SSO sign-in" (shorter). for per-role tooltip use "Requires SSO" not "Enforce". maya: sounds good. on the visual lock: variant 1 shows a small filled lock at start of row; variant 2 shows lightweight outline next to name. which reads clearer at small sizes? sam: outline reads cleaner with condensed UI. filled lock draws too much visual weight in dense lists. diego: implementation note: for virtualized lists, avoid embedding complex DOM in every row. render a simple `
